clue.text: Protective cladding needed if, say, going away to school

indicators.note: say tells us the word for if is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: if means whether, as in 'ask if he is coming'
a pupil going away to school is boarding there

explanation.surface: Someone says protection is needed when a child goes off to boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: WHETHER (if) sounds like WEATHER, then add BOARDING (going away to school).
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping horizontal planks fixed to an outside wall shield a house from rain and wind.

clue.text: Destroyer's crew at sea with king and queen

definitions.note: read as 'Destroyer is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of crew are jumbled

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the regular abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A warship's crew sail with royalty aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges CREW to WREC; add K and ER. The 's of Destroyer's is 'is', joining the definition to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ruins or wreaks havoc on things is a destroyer.

clue.text: Reckoned it's bad losing a pound

indicators.note: losing means the following item is dropped from the word for bad

parts.note: an addled egg is one that has gone bad
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone works out that things went wrong because a pound went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDLED (bad, of an egg) loses L (a pound) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up figures is to reckon or total them, so reckoned is the past tense.

clue.text: Boisterous behaviour from supporter before game

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: a horse is a frame that supports something, like a clothes horse or trestle
to play is to take part in a game; a play is also a game or sport

explanation.surface: Rowdiness from a team's fan ahead of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a football fan, but here it is a HORSE, a supporting frame such as a clothes horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough, rowdy fooling about is the boisterous conduct of children at play.

clue.text: Called for support for the chair

definitions.meaning: a crosspiece joining a chair's legs

explanation.definitionFit: Rang or telephoned is one sense; the other is a crossbar bracing the legs of seating.

clue.text: Look up English plant or evergreen

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for look is written bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'
the aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: Someone checks a botanical reference on an English plant or evergreen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' reads as a request to consult a reference, but 'up' turns the short word for look in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild olive, a shrub of the Mediterranean, keeps its silvery leaves all year.

clue.text: Australian bounder on the way to stay the night

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a kangaroo, roo for short, bounds across the Australian outback
ST, short for street, is a common crossword word for way

explanation.surface: A kangaroo on the road looking for a place to spend the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' suggests a cad, but here it is something that leaps: ROO, then ST (street, the way).
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch to sleep, so the verb means to bed down for the night.

clue.text: Start off sort of sports spectacle for audience

indicators.note: start off means the first letter of the following phrase is removed

parts.note: winter sports are a kind of sport, such as skiing
a view is a spectacle or sight

explanation.surface: Telling someone to kick off a sporting show for the crowd watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' removes the W from WINTER VIEW. 'audience' looks like the spectators, but it is a formal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal meeting with an important person, as granted by a monarch or pope, is a sit-down conversation.

clue.text: Reflected in the middle of surgery, and made an incision

indicators.note: the middle of picks out the central letter of the word surgery

parts.note: a surgeon who lanced a boil made an incision in it

explanation.surface: A surgeon thinks deeply mid-operation and cuts into a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' suggests thinking, but means bounced off, as a ball or light does. G is the central letter of SURGERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A light ray or a ball that strikes a surface at an angle and bounces off has deflected.

clue.text: Stamina is called for in French trip round old city

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: round means one word is placed around the other

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic
Ur is the ancient city of the Chaldeans in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A French trip round an ancient city needs plenty of staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' suggests a journey, but here it is a light dance, as in tripping the light fantastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying power, the capacity to keep going through long effort, is stamina.

clue.text: Roman town initially on seashore, though inland afterwards

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A Roman town once lay on the coast, but now stands back from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the port of ancient Rome has been left inland by the silting of the Tiber.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the harbour city of ancient Rome at the Tiber's mouth.

clue.text: Type or sort of bean

definitions.meaning: nature or temperament, as in 'people of that kind'
a red, ...-shaped variety of bean used in chilli

explanation.definitionFit: The word means kind or temperament, and it names a red bean shaped like the organ.

clue.text: One enters Crete's old resort intended for select few

indicators.note: enters means one letter goes inside the jumbled letters
re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A tourist arrives at an exclusive old Cretan holiday spot meant for the few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday spot, but means re-sort: CRETES plus O rearrange to ESOTERC, and I (one) enters it.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge understood only by a small inner circle of initiates is obscure and specialised.

clue.text: Run down part of army base

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
base means low or contemptible, the same as vile

explanation.surface: Part of an army base is in a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army base' looks like one phrase, a barracks; it splits into a corps of the army and a word for low or mean.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak abusively of someone is to disparage or criticise them.

clue.text: Propose true love — different name must be accepted

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or accept, the abbreviation for name
different means the letters of true love are made into something else

explanation.surface: A suitor proposes true love, but another name must be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges TRUE LOVE to VOLUTEER, and 'must be accepted' takes N (name) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest or put forward an idea or offer is to propose it.

clue.text: German dramatist, married with English family

parts.note: to wed is to marry, so wed means married
kind means family or kin, as in an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: A German playwright marries into an English family.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Wedekind (1864-1918) wrote Spring Awakening and the Lulu plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Wedekind was a German playwright, author of Spring Awakening.

clue.text: Special case that justifies the law

definitions.text: Special case that justifies the law

parts.words: Special case that justifies the law
parts.note: a play on the saying that the odd case which does not fit proves the rule, so a breach seems to justify a law

explanation.definitionFit: A case that does not follow the general pattern is an anomaly that stands outside the rule.

clue.text: Old chucker sends last bail flying

indicators.note: flying means the letters of last bail are sent scattering

explanation.surface: A ball sends the last bail flying off the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Bails sit on the cricket stumps; the surface is cricket, but 'flying' rearranges LAST BAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman siege engine hurled stones at walls, so it was an ancient throwing machine.

clue.text: Stray animal's cry, held back by a whip

definitions.note: read as 'Stray animal is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: held back means the word for cry is turned around

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: A homeless creature's cry is stopped by a lash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns the cry round to LLEY. The 's of animal's is 'is', joining the definition to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeless feline roaming city back streets is a stray creature.

clue.text: Record score

definitions.meaning: a written report or statement of events
reason or ground, as in 'on that score'

explanation.definitionFit: A report of events is one sense; 'on no score' and 'on no account' share the sense of grounds.

clue.text: Lowers boats holding 50

indicators.note: holding means the word for boats goes around the number

parts.note: scows are flat-bottomed boats
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone lets down boats carrying fifty passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' reads as lets down, but rhymes with 'flowers': it means frowns. SCOWS holds L (50).
explanation.definitionFit: To lour or lower is to look sullen, the same as to glower or frown.

clue.text: It's natural but wrong having religious education under the Church

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the last piece below the one before

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
CE is the Church of England
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Someone insists it is natural, but wrong, to have school religion beneath the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN (wrong), then CE (Church of England), with RE (religious education, a British school subject) under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and unaffected feeling, free of pretence, is honest and natural.

clue.text: Start to carve a head and neck

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word carve is taken

parts.note: noodle is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Instructions for a butcher to begin carving a head and neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' reads as a cut of meat, but is the verb meaning kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is to kiss and cuddle amorously, which is what courting couples do.

clue.text: Soldiers upset when expected to make speeches

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, is when someone is expected

explanation.surface: Disgruntled troops give speeches when they are due.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) then ETA, estimated time of arrival, turned up as ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver formal addresses in a pompous manner is to hold forth.

clue.text: Injury resulting from run in the country

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for run goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a country
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone hurt themselves going for a run in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' reads as rural land, but is a nation: SPAIN with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted ankle or wrenched ligament is a common hurt.

clue.text: Porter is in central part of carriage

indicators.note: in means the word is goes inside the word for porter

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway porter stands in the middle of a train carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a railway worker, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage running down the middle of a train coach between the seats is a walkway.

clue.text: One admired in lido when swimming

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of lido move about freely

explanation.surface: Someone people look up to is spotted taking a swim at the open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero worshipped by fans is a figure of devotion.

clue.text: Religious body involved in rule making

indicators.note: involved in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A church council is busy drafting regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'rULE MAking'.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of Muslim scholars learned in Islamic law and theology forms a religious authority.

clue.text: Party with children not the main affair

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest
issue means offspring or children

explanation.surface: A party with children present is not the main event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration, but means one side in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary matter, of less importance than the central question, is a distraction.

clue.text: Went off to a binge, I heard? Pretended not to notice

parts.note: milk that has gone off has turned sour
a blind is a drinking bout or binge

indicators.note: heard means the letter I is taken as it sounds, not as written

parts.note: the letter I said out loud is the word for an organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone went on a drinking spree, they say, and others looked the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the 'I' in 'I heard'. BLIND is an old British slang word for a drinking binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson put a telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal, so the phrase means deliberately overlooking something.
